stories.headline: China imposes export controls on tunnel-boring machines sought by India, cites ‘national security’
stories.title: China imposes export controls on tunnel-boring machines sought by India, cites ‘national security’
stories.summary: Announcement comes days after Beijing announced plans to impose export controls on 40 cutting-edge technologies, including those for advanced solar manufacturing, AI platforms
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'national security' in title weight 70
article_sentences: China on Monday said it would introduce export controls on tunnel-boring machines “to better safeguard national security and interests”, starting November 18.
India has already been facing difficulties in customs clearance and delays in importing TBMs from China for several critical infrastructure projects.

The latest announcement comes days after Beijing announced a plan to impose sweeping export controls on 40 cutting-edge technologies, including those for certain advanced solar manufacturing and some AI platforms.

The Chinese Commerce Ministry said on Monday in an announcement it was “introducing export controls on tunnel-boring machines and related items and optimising and adjusting export-control measures for certain dredgers and related items.” The measures will take effect on November 18.
The ministry said prior to the announcement, China had “notified the relevant countries and regions with which it has established export-control dialogue mechanisms.”
“The items covered by these measures have clear dual-use (civilian and military) characteristics,” the announcement said.

“The measures are intended to better safeguard national security and interests, while also enabling China to better fulfil its international obligations, including those related to non-proliferation”.

India has previously raised with China the delays in customs clearance for imports of TBMs, which are used in India for several critical projects including the construction of metro rail networks in cities, railway corridors and key tunnelling projects, including in border areas.
India is dependent on imports for the machines.
Difficulties in imports from China started in 2024.

In October of that year, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal had publicly raised the issue with visiting German Vice Chancellor Robert Habeck, pointing out that China was blocking the export of TBMs made by a German company in China.
On Monday, China also announced export control measures related to certain types of drones.

stories.headline: Flood Of Pleas By Employees Challenging Their Transfers Has Paralysed Govt Functioning: Rajasthan High Court
stories.title: Flood Of Pleas By Employees Challenging Their Transfers Has Paralysed Govt Functioning: Rajasthan High Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: While hearing a bunch of petitions by government employees, challenging their transfer orders, Rajasthan High Court observed that the government functioning was paralysed since most of the employees were not willing to join the transferred place of posting.
The bench of Justice Anoop Kumar Dhand further opined that maximum number of employees were approaching the Court for getting the transfer orders cancelled.
It was held that the jurisdiction of the Court under Article 226, is not to act as a second appellate authority over the transfer orders passed by the competent authority or the appellate tribunal.

“This Court is constrained to observe that there is a flood of writ petitions assailing the transfer orders…Maximum number of employees are approaching this Court and the Rajasthan Civil Services Appellate Tribunal (for short, 'the Tribunal') for getting their transfer orders stayed and cancelled on one pretext or the other, thereby bringing the administrative machinery to a standstill.”
4) In extreme case of hardship to life threatening disease effecting the service conditions.
“It is settled proposition of law that transfer is an incidence of service.
No employee has a vested right to remain posted at a particular place of his choice.

It is for the employer or the competent authority to decide as to where and how its employees are to be posted, considering the administrative exigencies, public interest and smooth functioning of the administration.”

While opining that no other ground could be valid for interfering in transfer orders, including personal inconveniences, hardship, long stay, etc., the Court held that no ground for interference was present in the present batch of petitions.

However, in order to balance equities, the Court granted liberty to the petitioners to file representations before competent authorities within 2 weeks, and directed the authorities to decide the same within further 2 weeks.
Accordingly, the transfer orders were stayed for 4 weeks.

stories.headline: 2 Election Commissioners wrote to Cabinet Secretary. RTI reveals what happened next
stories.title: 2 Election Commissioners wrote to Cabinet Secretary. RTI reveals what happened next
stories.summary: 2 Election Commissioners wrote to Cabinet Secretary. RTI reveals what happened next
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Two Election Commissioners wrote to the Cabinet Secretary over a disputed work-allocation order.
The RTI reply confirms the paper trail but leaves the letters' contents undisclosed.
On July 29, two of India’s three Election Commissioners did something unusual.
They didn’t write to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

A Right to Information (RTI) reply obtained exclusively by India Today reveals what happened to those letters inside Seva Teerth, the complex that houses the Prime Minister’s Office, the National Security Council Secretariat and the Cabinet Secretariat.
The reply, dated October 19, responds to an RTI application filed on September 24.
It confirms that the letters, one from Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and the other from Vivek Joshi, both dated July 29, reached the Cabinet Secretariat.
The two letters were logged on July 30, and by August 5, the Cabinet Secretary forwarded them to Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) officials and the CEC’s office.
The contents of the letters, however, remain undisclosed.
The Secretariat has withheld all 14 pages — comprising the Commissioners’ 10-page letters, two pages of replies and two pages of file notings — pending payment of a Rs 28 fee.
The trigger was a July 28 work-allocation order.
A newspaper reported that the two Commissioners objected to the order and wrote to the Cabinet Secretary, calling it a violation of rules.

stories.headline: Third Chair: Who Should Pick India's Election Commissioners
stories.title: Third Chair: Who Should Pick India's Election Commissioners
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: On 23 September, a two-judge Bench of the Supreme Court split on whether the challenge to the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 needs a Constitution Bench.
Justice Dipankar Datta held that Anoop Baranwal.
Union of India, had already settled the governing principles and that the Court needed only to test the 2023 law against them.

Justice Satish Chandra Sharma held that the question of whether Parliament could exclude a neutral selector from the appointment committee was a substantial question of constitutional interpretation arising for the first time, and that Article 145(3) reserves such questions for a larger Bench.
Both judges agreed that the papers should go to Chief Justice Surya Kant.
The question before the larger Bench is narrower than the political debate suggests, and harder.
It is not a question of whether Parliament could legislate.

Article 324(2) makes appointments by the President “subject to the provisions of any law made in that behalf by Parliament”, and the 2023 Constitution Bench said its own committee of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition, and the Chief Justice would hold good only until such a law was made.
At the hearing on reference, the Solicitor General argued that Anoop Baranwal prescribed an interim arrangement, not a constitutional requirement that the Chief Justice sit on the committee.
Justice Datta appears to accept part of that: had the Constitution Bench meant the Chief Justice's presence to be binding, he observed, it would have said so.
The live question is different.
It is whether the law Parliament actually made meets the standard of independence that Article 324 carries within it, and that Anoop Baranwal articulated.

stories.title: Supreme Court pauses CMRL bribery probe against Pinarayi Vijayan for a week
stories.summary: Supreme Court pauses CMRL bribery probe against Pinarayi Vijayan for a week
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court stayed the CMRL bribery investigation against Pinarayi Vijayan and his family for a week.
The pause enables them to challenge the FIR order before a Kerala High Court division bench.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday stayed for a week the investigation against former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan and his family members in the alleged CMRL bribery case, news agency Press Trust of India reported.
CPI(M) state secretary M V Govindan welcomed the decision, saying it upheld the rule of law.
State Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala, however, said the court had not set aside the FIR and claimed that the action taken by the Congress-led UDF government had been proved correct.
In a statement, Chennithala said the investigation had been stayed for a week to allow Vijayan and the others to file an appeal and argue the matter before the Kerala High Court.
Govindan told reporters that the Supreme Court's order was encouraging for the CPI(M), according to PTI.
He said the party had maintained from the beginning that the case was politically motivated and would be challenged both legally and politically.

Govindan claimed that the Supreme Court said the Kerala High Court should have considered the appeal filed by Vijayan, his daughter Veena T and her husband P. A Mohamed Riyas against the October 9 order directing the registration of an FIR against them.
“The rule of law has been upheld by the Supreme Court verdict,” he said.

Chennithala said the state government had carefully examined the Enforcement Directorate's letter seeking the registration of a case against Vijayan, Veena and Riyas under the Prevention of Corruption Act and had not acted in haste.
He said the government had sought legal advice and ordered a preliminary inquiry.

stories.headline: India-US trade deal may be weeks away, but tariff relief and certainty remain key: GTRI’s Srivastava
stories.title: India-US trade deal may be weeks away, but tariff relief and certainty remain key: GTRI’s Srivastava
stories.summary: As India and the US move closer to signing a trade agreement, Ajay Srivastava of GTRI says the key question is whether Washington will offer lower tariffs and protection against future duty hikes.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: An impending India-US trade deal could be finalised soon, with experts noting that tariff cuts, long-term trade certainty, and energy cooperation including Venezuelan crude supplies will be critical to the agreement's success and broader bilateral economic ties.

The proposed India-US trade agreement could be finalised within weeks, but the final outcome will depend on the tariff concessions and long-term trade certainty that Washington offers New Delhi, according to Ajay Srivastava, Founder of the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), and Pramit Pal Chaudhuri, Practice Head for South Asia at Eurasia Group.

Speaking after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the agreement was a matter of weeks, not months, both experts said investors and exporters should closely watch the final terms of the deal rather than the timeline.
They also said energy cooperation, including Venezuelan crude supplies and refinery investments, could become an important pillar of broader India-US economic ties.
"We don't know what the US is going to offer us.
We know what we are going to offer them because we have signed that February joint statement," Srivastava said.
He added that the biggest issue is whether Indian exports will receive lower tariff rates after the agreement.
Srivastava said the current tariff structure remains uncertain across several product categories.
While sectors such as pharmaceuticals and smartphones already enjoy exemptions, labour-intensive exports including garments, textiles and leather continue to face higher duties.
"For example, today our shirts going to the US pay 22% tariff.
After the trade deal, will this be 22% or less?" he said.
He added that exporters would also seek protection against future tariff increases, noting that the US had imposed additional duties on some countries even after signing trade agreements with them.

stories.headline: Supreme Court defers AP municipal poll final list to October 25 on YSRCP plea, directs SEC to decide on nominations
stories.title: Supreme Court defers AP municipal poll final list to October 25 on YSRCP plea, directs SEC to decide on nominations
stories.summary: The court holds that the YSRCP has made out a prima facie case in its plea for more time to file nominations
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) held that the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) had made out a prima facie case in its plea for an extension of time to file nominations for the urban local body elections in Andhra Pradesh.
The party had alleged that its candidates were met with violence and blocked from filing nominations.

The SEC was directed to consider the representations of the party and its candidates, including evidence and material as well as electronic evidence, and to take a decision on extending the last date for filing nominations in urban local bodies wherever it is of the view that candidates were unable to file.
The decision is to be taken by Thursday (October 22).
Wherever the SEC chooses to extend the time, the extension shall not be less than 48 hours from the publication of the decision, which is to be done by amending the election notification.
The Director General of Police (DGP) was directed to take all necessary steps to provide security, maintain CCTV footage and file a compliance report in the Supreme Court.
The SEC was also directed to take the necessary decisions and issue orders to remove apprehensions from the minds of the petitioner and all concerned, and to file a compliance report.
Nominations are also to be permitted at district headquarters.
The YSRCP, led by former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, had alleged that mass violence in the State prevented its candidates from filing nominations for the urban local body elections.

It sought police protection for candidates, an extension of the deadline for filing nominations and the designation of additional and alternative nomination centres to enable candidates to submit their papers safely.

The plea, filed by party general secretary Lella Appireddy through advocate Mahfooz Ahsan Nazki, said several of its candidates were allegedly assaulted and physically prevented from reaching nomination centres during the nomination period, which began on October 16 and ended on October 18.
The High Court had dismissed the party’s application seeking an extension, holding that the deadline had expired and that extending it would amount to interference with the election process.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Quashes Blacklisting Of Drug Supplier Over Quality Failure As Retesting Opportunity Denied
stories.title: Supreme Court Quashes Blacklisting Of Drug Supplier Over Quality Failure As Retesting Opportunity Denied
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has quashed the blacklisting of a pharmaceutical supplier by the Madhya Pradesh government after finding that the authorities failed to follow the mandatory procedure for retesting drug samples before imposing punitive action.

A bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Augustine George Masih and Sandeep Mehta set aside orders blacklisting M/s JPEE Drugs for three years and debarring it from supplying a particular drug for two years after four batches of medicines supplied by the firm were declared Not of Standard Quality (NSQ).

The Court held that the failure to conduct retesting in accordance with the tender conditions, followed by the authorities' failure to comply with the High Court's directions for fresh testing within the stipulated period, deprived the firm of an effective opportunity to challenge the laboratory reports.

"The procedural infirmity, coupled with the irretrievable deprivation of the opportunity for re-testing, renders the orders of blacklisting and debarment unsustainable in law," the Court observed in its October 6 judgment.

The case arose from the supply of Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C) tablets and Ethambutol Hydrochloride tablets to government hospitals and health centres in Madhya Pradesh by JPEE Drugs, a licensed pharmaceutical firm.
In September 2024, the firm received a show-cause notice after three batches of Vitamin C tablets and one batch of Ethambutol Hydrochloride tablets were declared NSQ in laboratory reports.
The firm denied supplying substandard medicines and contended that the quality failures could have resulted from improper storage and handling after delivery.

On September 30, 2024, the Managing Director of the Madhya Pradesh Public Health Services Corporation Limited (MPPHSCL) passed orders directing recovery of the value of the affected batches, blacklisting the firm for three years in respect of the Vitamin C tablets, and debarring it for two years from supplying the Ethambutol Hydrochloride tablets.
The orders stated that no reply had been received from the firm.
A subsequent order dated October 1, 2024, considered and rejected its representation and reiterated the blacklisting and debarment decisions.
Before the Supreme Court, the supplier argued that the authorities had acted without waiting for its reply to the show-cause notice, which had granted seven days to respond.

It also relied on Clause 6 of Annexure IX to the tender document, which required a second sample to be drawn from the same batch and sent to another laboratory if the initial test declared the drug to be of substandard quality.

opening: The Supreme Court has quashed the blacklisting of a pharmaceutical supplier by the Madhya Pradesh government after finding that the authorities failed to follow the mandatory procedure for retesting drug samples before imposing punitive action.

A bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Augustine George Masih and Sandeep Mehta set aside orders blacklisting M/s JPEE Drugs for three years and debarring it from supplying a particular drug for two years after four batches of medicines supplied by the firm were declared Not of Standard Quality (NSQ).
body: The Court held that the failure to conduct retesting in accordance with the tender conditions, followed by the authorities' failure to comply with the High Court's directions for fresh testing within the stipulated period, deprived the firm of an effective opportunity to challenge the laboratory reports.

"The procedural infirmity, coupled with the irretrievable deprivation of the opportunity for re-testing, renders the orders of blacklisting and debarment unsustainable in law," the Court observed in its October 6 judgment.

The case arose from the supply of Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C) tablets and Ethambutol Hydrochloride tablets to government hospitals and health centres in Madhya Pradesh by JPEE Drugs, a licensed pharmaceutical firm.
In September 2024, the firm received a show-cause notice after three batches of Vitamin C tablets and one batch of Ethambutol Hydrochloride tablets were declared NSQ in laboratory reports.
The firm denied supplying substandard medicines and contended that the quality failures could have resulted from improper storage and handling after delivery.

On September 30, 2024, the Managing Director of the Madhya Pradesh Public Health Services Corporation Limited (MPPHSCL) passed orders directing recovery of the value of the affected batches, blacklisting the firm for three years in respect of the Vitamin C tablets, and debarring it for two years from supplying the Ethambutol Hydrochloride tablets.
The orders stated that no reply had been received from the firm.
A subsequent order dated October 1, 2024, considered and rejected its representation and reiterated the blacklisting and debarment decisions.
